Three AI consulting companies to assess for handover

Pick a company whose delivery team can leave your operators with a working system. A reference call is most useful when someone who ran the system after launch joins it. These cases suggest three different handover exercises.

We chose these examples for the specific work documented in a client case or product guide. Client outcomes are provider-reported. AY Automate publishes this guide.

  1. WeAreBrain · An ERP workflow with external partners

    WeAreBrain names both Truck Tyre Assist and the ERP partner on its breakdown-operations project. Ask a potential delivery team to map ownership of a supplier notification that fails after dispatch. Your operator should be able to find the case, determine its status and reach the right support contact.

    Read the source from WeAreBrain

  2. Slalom · A service desk used across regions

    Genie’s contact-center project with Slalom covered technology and change management. Ask the bidder to let a supervisor change a queue rule in staging using the written handover. Time the exercise and record where the supervisor needed vendor help. Those gaps belong in the last delivery milestone.

    Read the source from Slalom

  3. Capgemini · An automation program shared by business units

    ZF and Capgemini established a global RPA service. Use the example to ask how a newly hired process owner learns to propose, test and retire an automation. Request a walkthrough of the approval record, the rollback instructions and the person responsible for the next improvement.

    Read the source from Capgemini

What to ask before you buy

  1. If your engineers will take over, ask for a sample repository, runbook and handover schedule.
  2. If the provider will operate the system, agree on incident coverage, escalation and the cost of changes.
  3. Identify who owns evaluation data, infrastructure accounts and deployment access from day one.

Rehearse the handover of an AI application

Ask your own operator to deploy, diagnose and roll back the application while the delivery team observes.

How to compare prices

Compare build-and-handover with managed operation over twelve months. Include your own engineers’ time, vendor support and migration costs.

A worked example to review

McKinsey explains its hybrid intelligence approach in terms of the role people play alongside technology. Use that discussion to specify who owns decisions in your deployment.

Read the provider’s example

Who should own the code and infrastructure accounts?

Write the arrangement into the contract. A team that expects to take over needs repository access, operating instructions and a tested way to deploy independently.
